correctness.rationale: For a zero-labeled vertex in part \(V_i\), the neighborhood is exactly the complement of \(V_i\), so the defining condition is equivalent to \(B-b_i\ge1\) or \(A-a_i\ge2\). The proof partitions all labelings into three disjoint regimes by the part-support of label 2, and the no-2 regime is counted by a complete classification of the only possible failures. No finite computation is used to infer the infinite result. The packaged verifier independently checked every part-size profile through order 10, totaling 3,169,350 labelings.

value.rationale: The result gives the complete weight distribution for a standard infinite graph family and converts an exponential all-labeling census into coefficient extraction from an explicit part-size formula. It strictly refines scalar domination numbers: for example, \(K_{1,3}\) and \(K_{1,1,2}\) both have order 4 and minimum weight 2, but their weight-2 coefficients are 1 and 4, respectively. Thus the enumerator records genuine structural information invisible to the known minimum value and can support probabilistic or reliability questions about nonminimum feasible defenses.
